answer: This design pays newcomers on a lotus schedule, not in full at once: 10 percent in epoch one, 30 in epoch two, 60 in epoch three, full rate only from epoch four. Each step needs a receipt for work at the wharf that epoch; an idle identity stalls, so the k-th fake needs four epochs of upkeep: 1,000 fakes need 1,000 histories and 4,000 receipts, while an honest newcomer climbs once. The named failure mode is aging farms: scripts warming idle accounts stall, because each receipt must be quill-signed for real work for a real client and is single-use across identities.
